{"metadata":{"description":"Structural long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness: supersede/decay/entity-state store, 15 MCP memory tools, automatic recall, bounded context band","id":"gh:1397075782","install_available":true,"language":"Python","name":"dsh-flymemory","slug":"aujurd22/dsh-flymemory","topics":["agent-memory","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-bundle","dsh-plugin","flymemory","long-term-memory","mcp","memory"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Structural long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness: supersede/decay/entity-state store, 15 MCP memory "},{"id":"p1s2","text":"tools, automatic recall, bounded context band"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-flymemory"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"Long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness —
the kind that also remembers **what changed**."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"You know the feeling. New session, and you explain the project again: what it is, what
we decided, w"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"hat we tried, what broke. Ten minutes later the model confidently hands you
a plan you abandoned thr"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"ee weeks ago, because that plan is still in its memory and
nothing in the store knows it stopped bei"},{"id":"p5s4","text":" ago, because that plan is still in its memory and
nothing in the store knows it stopped being true."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"That last part is what this plugin is about. Most memory tools solve "remember more".
This one also "},{"id":"p6s2","text":"solves "stop believing the old version"."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"## Try it"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"Then in DSH just ask something you discussed in another session. If it answers with
context you didn"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"'t give it, it's working."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"Two things happen on install:"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"- the first start takes **~10–13 seconds** (the embedding model loads); after that the
service stays"},{"id":"p11s2","text":" up and answers in milliseconds;
- the very first install also downloads a **915 MB** multilingual e"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"mbedding model, once."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"Everything stays on your machine: one library file and one ledger, both under
`$DSH_HOME/flymemory-d"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"ata`. Nothing is sent anywhere."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"## What it actually does"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"| | what you get |"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"| **Remembers across sessions and clients** | ZCode, Qoder and DSH can share one library; each entry"},{"id":"p15s2","text":" is tagged with the client that wrote it, so the recall can say who told whom |
| **Knows what's out"},{"id":"p15s3","text":" of date** | when a fact changes, the old entry is *retired*, not deleted: it keeps `valid_from`/`va"},{"id":"p15s4","text":"lid_to` and the entry that replaced it, and stops showing up in normal recall |
| **Answers "why did"},{"id":"p15s5","text":" I think that back then"** | the retired entry is still there with its dates, so the history is insp"},{"id":"p15s6","text":"ectable instead of overwritten |
| **Keeps the per-turn cost small** | each turn injects a bounded i"},{"id":"p15s7","text":"ndex (≤1.2 KB) of pointers; the model pulls the full text only for what it needs |
| **Shows what go"},{"id":"p15s8","text":"t used** | `usegate.jsonl` records every injected pointer, whether it was expanded, recalled again, "},{"id":"p15s9","text":"or superseded — you can finally see whether the memory is doing anything |
| **Cleans up after itsel"},{"id":"p15s10","text":"f** | daily pass: merge duplicates with the model, retire stale state, fold groups, shrink the file "},{"id":"p15s11","text":"** | daily pass: merge duplicates with the model, retire stale state, fold groups, shrink the file |"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"## The three things you'll use most"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"And when you want it to think about itself:"},{"id":"p19s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"## Why not just a note table with cosine search"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"A note table stores text and finds similar text. That covers half the job. The other
half is knowing"},{"id":"p21s2","text":" which of those notes is still true."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"| | note table + cosine | dsh-flymemory |"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"| a fact changed | old and new both come back | the old one is retired and hidden from recall |
| th"},{"id":"p23s2","text":"e same thing said twice | piles up | length-tiered dedup merges or strengthens |
| "what is X *now*""},{"id":"p23s3","text":" | you write the query | `state_key` keeps the current value plus its chain of previous values |
| a"},{"id":"p23s4","text":"ge | everything looks equally fresh | power-law decay weights by retention |
| where it came from | "},{"id":"p23s5","text":"lost | `source` and `app:<name>` on every entry |
| did it help | unknown | the usage ledger |"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"## Waking up once a day"},{"id":"p25s1","text":"A per-window pass can't see that two topics are the same thing. A whole-store rewrite
can, but it ri"},{"id":"p25s2","text":"sks drift. The daily pass sits in between: it reads a bounded digest
(8 topic buckets × 12 entries),"},{"id":"p25s3","text":" asks the model for at most three durable conclusions
plus redundant pairs, and writes them as **one"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"** playbook entry — yesterday's playbook
is retired into it, so there is always exactly one current "},{"id":"p25s5","text":" entry — yesterday's playbook
is retired into it, so there is always exactly one current macro view."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"On Windows it's a scheduled task at 04:30; elsewhere, a cron line:"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"## How well it works"},{"id":"p29s1","text":"Short version: on a public long-memory benchmark (LongMemEval oracle, 120 questions,
same reader and"},{"id":"p29s2","text":" judge for every arm), this plugin's protocol scored **69.2%** where
plain retrieval scored 50.8%, u"},{"id":"p29s3","text":"sing about a third of the tokens that pasting the whole
history costs. Against a widely used memory "},{"id":"p29s4","text":"library it's a **tie** (58.3% vs 56.7%)."},{"id":"p30s1","text":"Things it is *not*: smarter than the model, better than reading everything when the
history is short"},{"id":"p30s2","text":", or good at guessing your preferences. The full numbers, the protocols
and the negative results are"},{"id":"p30s3","text":" in docs/COMPARISON.md — including
one we falsified ourselves ("few but dense" notes do not work for"},{"id":"p30s4","text":".md — including
one we falsified ourselves ("few but dense" notes do not work for raw conversation)."},{"id":"p31s1","text":"## Honest limits"},{"id":"p32s1","text":"- **One writer at a time.** The service serialises writes; two processes pointed at the
same file wi"},{"id":"p32s2","text":"ll fight, and the second one now writes a `*.conflict-<time>` copy instead
of silently clobbering.
-"},{"id":"p32s3","text":" **Preferences are weak.** The benchmark says so; don't expect a profile feature.
- **Heavier than a"},{"id":"p32s4","text":" pure-JS plugin.** Python plus a 915 MB model, versus a SQLite file.
If you want zero dependencies, "},{"id":"p32s5","text":"there are simpler options.
- **Recall is top-k.** An entry that is semantically distant won't come b"},{"id":"p32s6","text":"ack; that's
retrieval, not a bug we can wish away."},{"id":"p33s1","text":"## Requirements"},{"id":"p34s1","text":"- DeepSeek Harness (this is a bundle plugin)
- Python 3.10+ with `torch` and `sentence-transformers`"},{"id":"p34s2","text":" (the CLI finds it for you and
`doctor` tells you if it can't)
- Node 20+"},{"id":"p35s1","text":"## Configuration"},{"id":"p36s1","text":"Set in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or leave the defaults:"},{"id":"p37s1","text":"| key | default | what it does |"},{"id":"p38s1","text":"| `port` | `8791` | where the memory service listens |
| `libraryPath` | under the data dir | which "},{"id":"p38s2","text":"library to use (point several clients at one) |
| `workingContextChars` | `1200` | size of the point"},{"id":"p38s3","text":"er index injected each turn |
| `workingContextRefreshMs` | `45000` | how often that index refreshes"},{"id":"p38s4","text":" |
| `recallProtocol` | `true` | the "pull what you need" prompt section |
| `answerProtocol` | `tru"},{"id":"p38s5","text":"e` | the "extract facts, then compute" section |
| `checkpointContract` | `true` | fold compaction s"},{"id":"p38s6","text":"ummaries back into memory |"}],"truncated":true}
